candidates.old:
LDY #&08
    STY sysvia_orb                  \ and high again
    LDY #4
.wait_high
    DEY
    BNE wait_high
    RTS
candidates.new:
LDA #&08
    STA sysvia_orb                  \ and high again (Y is still 0)
    RTS
    SKIP 5                          \ the old recovery delay's bytes, so nothing after moves
candidates.summary: sfx_write: drop the post-write-enable-high delay loop (LDY #4 / DEY / BNE: 21 cycles of 27 in the tail) and write the high with LDA #8 / STA so Y stays 0; 5 bytes padded with SKIP 5 so no later code in bank 5 moves a byte.
candidates.equivalence: sfx_write's tail: A is dead on return (every caller reloads A: sfx_output's tone/noise paths start LDA sfx_p_hi / LDA sfx_v, sfx_tick's callers go to DEX or LDA sfx_dp,X; the dataflow out: at the RTS is XYCV), C and X are untouched, Y is still 0 from wait_low's exit (as before: the old wait_high also ended at Y=0, and sfx_next_ramp.ended's comment says so), Z/N are dead. Write enable high is written with A instead of Y (same 2+4 cycles, same VIA write cycle). Only the recovery delay after the rising edge goes: the chip's constraint is write enable low for >=8us (wait_low, 17 cycles from STZ's write to the high write, untouched); after the rise, the data bus is next changed by a STA sysvia_ora_nh no earlier than 31 cycles later on any path (RTS 6 + the caller's amplitude/period arithmetic or sfx_silence's loop, counted per path: tone low->high 44, high->amplitude 31, noise->amplitude 33, silence 44), and by the main program or the MOS only after RTS/RTS/PLA/STA/PLA/PLY/PLX/RTI.
candidates.relies_on: No label after sfx_write moves (SKIP 5 keeps .noise at &A5A4 and everything after it where it was), so no page crossing changes anywhere in bank 5; sfx_write itself stays inside page &A5 (&A589-&A5A3), branch wait_low is still in-page, BEQ noise unchanged. Relies on the SN76489 needing only the write-enable-low hold (wait_low kept at 17 cycles) and no hold after the rising edge: every path has >=31 cycles between the rise and the next chip write, so a 8us recovery is covered without the loop. wait_high is referenced nowhere else (grep src/ tools/). This is a hardware-timing change the emulator cannot show; MOS 3.20's own writes are not followed by this delay inside its routine on any path that matters.

candidates.old:
STY sysvia_orb                  \ and high again
    LDY #4
candidates.new:
STY sysvia_orb                  \ and high again
    LDY #2
candidates.summary: Conservative alternative (overlaps the first two): keep the structure and shorten the post-high delay loop from 4 to 2 passes (19 -> 9 cycles), same bytes, nothing moves.
candidates.equivalence: Only the number of iterations of a pure DEY/BNE delay changes; the loop still exits with Y=0, Z=1, N=0 and leaves A, X, C, V alone, so register and flag state at the RTS is identical. The recovery after the write-enable rise falls from 27 to 17 cycles (LDY, loop, RTS: 2+9+6) before any following chip write, and every path then spends >=31 more cycles before the next STA sysvia_ora_nh, so the gap from the rise to the next chip write is >=48 cycles (24us) against the chip's 8us (32 clocks at 4 MHz).
candidates.relies_on: No byte moves (LDY #4 and LDY #2 are both two bytes), so no page crossing changes; the loop stays inside &A59E-&A5A3 on page &A5. wait_low (the 8us write-enable hold) is untouched. Hardware timing the emulator cannot show; this is the minimal-risk way to take cycles from the delay.
